status: Proposed evidence for owner review; independent clinical and pharmacy review remains pending

00102.title: Chapman et al. BRIM-3, NEJM 2011
00102.population: 675 previously untreated patients with metastatic BRAF V600E melanoma
00102.design: Randomised vemurafenib 960 mg twice daily versus dacarbazine 1000 mg/m² every three weeks
00102.results: At the 2011 analysis, six-month overall survival was 84% versus 64%; response was 48% versus 5%.
limitations: Early historical analysis; later crossover and subsequent treatment affect longer-term comparisons.
Dacarbazine comparator, not a modern BRAF/MEK combination or checkpoint regimen.

00237.title: Hauschild et al. BREAK-3, Lancet 2012
00237.population: 250 previously untreated patients with unresectable stage III or stage IV BRAF V600E melanoma
00237.design: Randomised 3:1 dabrafenib 150 mg twice daily versus dacarbazine 1000 mg/m² every three weeks
00237.results: Median progression-free survival was 5.1 versus 2.7 months; hazard ratio 0.30, 95% CI 0.18–0.51.
limitations: Advanced-disease monotherapy evidence, not postoperative dabrafenib/trametinib evidence.
The comparator and treatment era do not establish superiority over current combinations.

00373.title: Ascierto et al. coBRIM, Lancet Oncology 2016
00373.population: 495 previously untreated patients with advanced BRAF V600-mutated melanoma
00373.design: Randomised cobimetinib plus vemurafenib versus placebo plus vemurafenib
00373.endpoint: Updated progression-free survival and final overall survival
00373.results: Median progression-free survival: 12.3 versus 7.2 months (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.46–0.72). Median overall survival: 22.3 versus 17.4 months (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.55–0.90).
limitations: Direct comparison was against vemurafenib alone.
It does not rank this regimen against other BRAF/MEK pairs or immunotherapy.

00105.title: Hodi et al., NEJM 2010
00105.population: Previously treated HLA-A*0201-positive patients with unresectable stage III or stage IV melanoma
00105.design: Three-arm randomised trial; the relevant comparison is ipilimumab 3 mg/kg alone (137 patients) versus gp100 vaccine alone (136)
00105.results: Median overall survival for ipilimumab alone was 10.1 versus 6.4 months with gp100; HR 0.66, p=0.003.
limitations: Historical gp100 comparator and selected previously treated population.
Do not substitute the separate ipilimumab-plus-gp100 arm or compare indirectly with modern PD-1 treatment.

00535/merkel_cell.title: Kaufman et al. JAVELIN Merkel 200 Part A, Lancet Oncology 2016
00535/merkel_cell.population: 88 patients with metastatic Merkel-cell carcinoma previously treated with chemotherapy
00535/merkel_cell.design: Single-arm phase 2 avelumab 10 mg/kg every two weeks
00535/merkel_cell.results: 28 of 88 patients responded (31.8%): eight complete and twenty partial responses; 23 of 28 responses were ongoing at the analysis.
limitations: No randomised comparator or demonstrated comparative survival advantage.
Trial dose was weight-based; current NCCP uses 800 mg.
First-line Part B is a different population and must not replace Part A for this source indication.

00551/melanoma.title: Lebbé et al. CheckMate 511, Journal of Clinical Oncology 2019
00551/melanoma.population: 360 previously untreated patients with unresectable stage III or stage IV melanoma
00551/melanoma.design: Randomised nivolumab 3 mg/kg + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg versus nivolumab 1 mg/kg + ipilimumab 3 mg/kg, four three-weekly doses then nivolumab
00551/melanoma.endpoint: Primary: grade 3–5 treatment-related adverse events; efficacy was descriptive
00551/melanoma.results: Grade 3–5 treatment-related adverse events occurred in approximately 34% versus 48% (p=0.006).
limitations: The study was not designed to establish efficacy noninferiority or equivalent survival.
Do not assign CheckMate 067 long-term survival estimates for the other dose combination to this schedule.
NCCP states the melanoma 3/1 dosing posology is unlicensed in Ireland; local consent and governance requirements apply.

00464.title: Robert et al. CheckMate 066, NEJM 2015 — historical context only
00464.population: 418 previously untreated patients with metastatic BRAF-wild-type melanoma
00464.design: Randomised nivolumab versus dacarbazine 1000 mg/m² every three weeks
00464.endpoint: Overall survival; response as secondary context
00464.results: The dacarbazine comparator response rate was 13.9%; this is not a validated efficacy estimate for NCCP dacarbazine 850 mg/m².
limitations: Dacarbazine dose differs from NCCP 00464, and the population was BRAF wild type.
The study primarily established benefit of nivolumab over a historical comparator.
No exact survival or response prediction is assigned to the NCCP 850 mg/m² course.

patient_reference.role: Education only; not Irish prescribing authority and not a Merkel-cell-specific source.

source_conflicts.issue: NCCP v6 holds at fever ≥38.5°C; current EMA Tafinlar PI §4.2/4.4 (updated 19 May 2026) says hold at ≥38°C for monotherapy. Patient proposal uses current PI 38°C and explicit clinician reconciliation.

NCCP linked old 100 mg SmPC has outdated reproductive advice. Current HPRA 200 mg SmPC March 2024 specifies women six months, men three months after last dose; NCCP 850 mg/m²/one-hour infusion/six-cycle schedule retained.
NCCP p13 footnote i declares melanoma 3/1 posology unlicensed in Ireland despite reimbursement; informed consent and hospital D&T or equivalent acknowledgement required.

not_authored: Fixed scan or tumour-marker intervals unsupported by the actual regimen
Equivalence of modern regimens inferred from separate historical studies
